summary: Citizens of the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the countries of Europe, Russia, China, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Turkey, Egypt and the Gulf states can obtain a 30-day visa on arrival (about US$51) at Dhaka and other international airports, while other nationalities — including Indian citizens — must arrange a visa through a Bangladeshi mission, starting on the official portal visa.gov.bd, before traveling. Maldivian citizens are visa-free under a bilateral agreement, and the immigration police say citizens of Barbados, Bhutan, Fiji, Grenada, Jamaica, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Trinidad and Tobago need no visa for stays of up to 90 days.

fee.notes: Paid on arrival in foreign currency (US dollars, pounds or euros). The 2016 circular does not print the amount; US$51 is the figure in common use. Nationals whose visas are fee-exempt pay nothing.

source.name: Security Services Division, Ministry of Home Affairs — Visa Policy (2006, amended to 2016) including the visa-on-arrival circular
source.instrument: Ministry of Home Affairs circular 44.00.0000.039.19.001.12-1409 of 15 September 2016 (visa on arrival), reinstated by Security Services Division circular 58.00.0000.041.01.002.22-59 of 17 May 2022

fee.notes: Set per nationality by the fee schedule published on visa.gov.bd — for a single-entry visa, for example, US$160 for US citizens, US$65 for British, US$50 for Japanese and Kenyan, US$15 for German citizens, and less or nothing for some. US$50 is only a common value.

source.name: Department of Immigration and Passports — Bangladesh Online MRV (visa) portal and visa fee schedule

fee.notes: Set per nationality by the fee schedule on visa.gov.bd (the multiple-entry column applies); needs a trade-association certificate or a Bangladeshi sponsor's recommendation. Issued for up to one year with stays of up to two months per visit.

source.name: Security Services Division, Ministry of Home Affairs — Visa Policy (2006, amended to 2016)
source.instrument: Visa Policy 2006 as amended by Ministry of Home Affairs circular of 30 December 2008 (B and T visa classes)

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months after the date your visa starts — and a Bangladeshi visa starts on its date of issue, not on your date of travel. It also needs at least 2 blank pages and no damage.

source.name: UK FCDO — Bangladesh entry requirements

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, or who transited through an airport in one — however short the transit.

source.name: WHO — International Travel and Health country list: vaccination requirements (Bangladesh)

travelInsurance.text: Not required for entry, but advisable — private hospitals in Dhaka are adequate for routine care, while serious cases are often evacuated to Bangkok or Singapore.

source.name: Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs — official visa portal

onwardTicket.text: Visa-on-arrival travelers must show a return or onward ticket; embassy-visa holders may also be asked by airlines at check-in.

source.name: Security Services Division, Ministry of Home Affairs — Visa Policy (2006, amended to 2016) including the visa-on-arrival circular
source.instrument: Ministry of Home Affairs circular 44.00.0000.039.19.001.12-1409 of 15 September 2016 (visa on arrival), reinstated by Security Services Division circular 58.00.0000.041.01.002.22-59 of 17 May 2022

proofOfFunds.text: Visa-on-arrival travelers must carry at least US$500 or the equivalent in foreign currency, in cash or on a credit card (official visits excepted), under the 2016 Home Ministry circular. Embassy-visa holders are not covered by that rule.

source.name: Security Services Division, Ministry of Home Affairs — Visa Policy (2006, amended to 2016) including the visa-on-arrival circular
source.instrument: Ministry of Home Affairs circular 44.00.0000.039.19.001.12-1409 of 15 September 2016 (visa on arrival), reinstated by Security Services Division circular 58.00.0000.041.01.002.22-59 of 17 May 2022

declarations.name: Arrival card
declarations.text: A paper arrival/disembarkation card is handed out on the plane or at the airport and must be completed for immigration.

source.name: Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs — official visa portal

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency over US$10,000 (or equivalent) must be declared to Customs on arrival on Form FMJ. Up to Tk 5,000 in Bangladeshi taka may be brought in or taken out without a declaration.

source.name: Bangladesh Bank — FE Circular No. 06 of 3 February 2020 (import and export of currency notes)
source.instrument: Bangladesh Bank Notification No. FE-1/2020-BB of 3 February 2020 (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947, s.8(1))

notes: Alcohol is restricted — non-Muslim foreign visitors may bring a small quantity for personal use; confirm the current allowance before travel.
Satellite phones require prior authorization and are seized at the border without it.

payments.text: Cards work at upmarket hotels, restaurants and malls in Dhaka and Chattogram, but Bangladesh runs on cash and mobile money (bKash). Carry taka for markets, rickshaws and everything outside the big cities.

safety.text: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks, political demonstrations and strikes can turn violent, and violent crime in Dhaka and other cities has risen since the 2024 uprising. Avoid protests and large gatherings, and take care on public transport at night. The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to the Chittagong Hill Tracts (Rangamati, Khagrachari and Bandarban).

source.name: UK FCDO — Bangladesh travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February is dry and relatively cool — the best window for Dhaka, the Sundarbans and Cox's Bazar. The monsoon (roughly June–October) brings heavy rain and flooding, with cyclone risk in the Bay of Bengal either side of it.

idp.text: Bangladesh is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Bangladesh is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Bangladesh yet.

tips.text: For the visa on arrival, carry the fee (about US$51) in exact US dollar cash, plus printed hotel bookings and your return ticket. The counter takes no cards and officers ask for supporting documents.

Political demonstrations and hartals (general strikes) can erupt with little notice, turn violent and paralyze transport. Avoid all rallies and processions, and build slack into travel plans around election periods and political anniversaries.

The June–October monsoon regularly floods roads and delays flights, and cyclones can strike coastal areas (including Cox's Bazar) in April–May and October–November — monitor forecasts in those windows.
Foreigners need prior permission from the authorities to visit the Chittagong Hill Tracts (Rangamati, Khagrachhari, Bandarban) — arrange it well ahead through a tour operator, and expect checkpoints.
Dress conservatively, especially outside Dhaka's affluent districts, and during Ramadan eat, drink and smoke discreetly in public during daylight hours.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bangladesh?
faq.answer: Almost everyone needs one, but many tourists get it at the airport: citizens of the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the countries of Europe, Russia, China, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Turkey, Egypt and the Gulf states can obtain a 30-day visa on arrival for about US$51. Other nationalities apply through a Bangladeshi mission, starting online at visa.gov.bd, where the fee schedule lists the fee for each nationality. Maldivian citizens are visa-free under a bilateral agreement, and the immigration police say citizens of Barbados, Bhutan, Fiji, Grenada, Jamaica, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Trinidad and Tobago need no visa for stays of up to 90 days.

faq.question: How does Bangladesh's visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: Eligible travelers pay the fee (about US$51) in US dollars, pounds or euros at Dhaka or another international airport or land port, for a single-entry stay of up to 30 days. Bring a return air ticket, hotel details and at least US$500 in cash or on a credit card — these are conditions of the 2016 circular, and issuance is at the officer's discretion, so confirm eligibility with your airline before flying.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Bangladesh?
faq.answer: Yes — visa extensions are handled by the Department of Immigration and Passports in Dhaka (Agargaon). Apply before your current stay expires; tourist stays are typically extended by up to 30 days at a time.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Bangladesh?
faq.answer: Yes — Indian passport holders are not eligible for the visa on arrival and must obtain a visa in advance from a Bangladeshi mission in India. Apply well before travel, as processing times and requirements change.

faq.question: Is Bangladesh safe to visit?
faq.answer: Most trips are trouble-free, and Bangladeshis are famously hospitable. The realistic risks are road accidents, petty crime in crowded areas and political unrest. Avoid demonstrations, use reputable transport, and check your government's latest advice before you go.
